Agent Skills are reusable workflows that guide your agent through SEO tasks using the MCP. - [Set up OpenSEO MCP](https://openseo.so/docs/mcp) - [Set up OpenSEO Agent Skills](https://openseo.so/docs/skills/setup) ## Self-Hosting OpenSEO supports two self-hosting paths: - **Simple: Docker (Best for testing it out)** - For personal use on your own machine. items.title: Agents in Orbit: Workflows, Not Autopilot — Eduardo Simon & Javier Casal, Flywire
items.summary: More than 9,700 code review runs in 30 days came from a workflow that lets the model read code but never modify it. Eduardo Simon and Javier Casal describe Orbit, Flywire's internal platform for putting model steps inside deterministic engineering workflows. A YAML definition goes through the same merge request review as other code, declares the tools and access each step can use, and runs on the company's existing deployment infrastructure. The predictable work stays in code; a model supplies the judgment. Human review of merge requests remains part of the process as the platform expands across roughly 400 engineers. Code review, translation updates, dependency fixes, ticket triage and bulk repository changes show the range of tasks this pattern supports. The architecture separates orchestration, execution and session state, then adds timeouts, rate limits and locks against duplicate runs. Per step restrictions cover network access, tools, skills and MCP servers, while structured outputs drive subsequent branches. The speakers are candid about the remaining work: new workflows initially receive a few real case checks, golden datasets run on demand, online evaluations are still being built and full sandboxing is a goal. Their reported execution success rate does not establish answer correctness. The practical adoption path starts with a useful skill, proves the recurring task and then turns it into a background workflow with explicit ownership and review. Speaker info…

items.title: Meta Muse AI Connectors: The App Store for AI?
items.summary: In this solo episode, I break down the huge business opportunity because Meta has opened Muse, its personal AI agent, to developers. You can now submit a connector, which lets Muse use your service when someone asks it for help, and I think this could be the app store moment for AI. I explain how a connector works, share four startup ideas you can build on one, and cover how to get customers beyond Meta's directory. I also show how I'd build a first version with a coding agent like Claude Code or Codex, and what I'd test before submitting it to Meta for review.
